blocks.text:
I was built for runoff, cigarette ash
For winters breaking glass in the street
I’ve taken oil, I’ve taken trash
Never learned the taste of blood in my teeth

They said it clears, they said it flows
Everything goes where it’s told
But this runs thicker, this runs slow
Warm and red in the midday cold

There’s something happening here
No rumor left to save
Broad daylight on the pavement
I’m choking on the blood you made

Boots step over what won’t move
Radios hum their steady tune
Orders land, a finger pulls
Someone drops, the street goes cold

I was made to hide the proof
Keep the surface clean
But you can’t rinse away a life
Once you’ve watched it leave

There’s something happening here
Not a question anymore
If the street can taste the truth
What are we waiting for?

I don’t get a vote
I don’t draw the line
But I carry the proof
Every goddamn time

There’s something happening here
Clear as sirens, clear as day
If even the drain is gagging now
What do we think we washed away?

notebook.style: Angry, ritual-driven alternative rock with a powerful percussive build, Mid-tempo in a minor mode, Drums are primal and physical: heavy toms, stomps, claps, Bass pulses underneath like a heartbeat, Guitar is sparse and textural, Song begins restrained and tense, then builds into fury and release through repetition and massed voices, Verse 1: minimal percussion, low drone, close vocal — controlled, watchful, Pre-Chorus: drums enter lightly, tension tightens, Chorus: full percussion hits; vocal expands into a commanding chant, Verse 2: drums heavier, claps join, delivery sharper and angrier, Bridge: strip to drums and voice only; raw, confrontational, Final Chorus: full return with layered voices chanting in unison; cathartic but unresolved, Outro: abrupt stop, No fade, No polish, No safety, Physical, communal anger
